paper.title: Optimal Regret Analysis of Thompson Sampling in Stochastic Multi-armed Bandit Problem with Multiple Plays

settings.name_in_paper: Multiple-play multi-armed bandit (MP-MAB) problem with Bernoulli rewards
unmapped: Action set is all subsets of exactly L < K arms (uniform matroid); total reward is the sum of the selected arms' rewards; m = L
settings.definition_quote: Each arm $i \in [K]$ is associated with a probability distribution $\nu_i = \Bernoulli(\mu_i)$, $\mu_i \in (0,1)$. At each round $t=1,2,\dots,T$, the forecaster selects a set of $L < K$ arms $I(t)$, then receives the rewards of the selected arms.

bound.regime: for any sufficiently small eps_1 > 0, eps_2 > 0

symbols.Delta_iL: mu_L - mu_i, gap between the L-th best arm and suboptimal arm i
symbols.mu_L: mean of the L-th best arm
symbols.L: number of arms selected per round (m)
symbols.C_a: constant independent of T, O(eps_1^{-2}) treating means as constants
symbols.C_b: function of T that grows as O(log log T) for proper choice of eps_2

conditions: mu_L is distinct: mu_{L-1} > mu_L > mu_{L+1} (Appendix: other ties allowed)
tuning: uniform Beta(1,1) prior on each arm

source.label: thm:mainregret
source.quote: For any sufficiently small $\epsilonOne>0, \epsilon_2>0$, the regret of MP-TS is upper-bounded as \Expect[\Regret(T)] \leq \sum_{i \in \subopts} \left( \frac{(1+\epsilonOne) \Delta_{i,L} \log{T}}{d(\mu_i, \mu_L)} \right) + C_a(\epsilonOne, \mu_1,\mu_2,\dots,\mu_K) + C_b(T, \epsilon_2, \mu_1,\mu_2,\dots,\mu_K), where, $C_a$ is a constant independent on $T$ and is $O(\epsilonOne^{-2})$ ... $C_b$ ... grows at a rate of $O(\log \log{T}) = o(\log{T})$.

results.notes: Sum is over suboptimal arms i in [K]\[L]; d is Bernoulli KL. Regret defined via means, hence pseudo-regret. Paper then sets eps_1 = O((log T)^{-1/3}) to get sum Delta_{i,L} log T / d(mu_i,mu_L) + O((log T)^{2/3}), matching Anantharam et al. lower bound; also derives asymptotic high-probability optimality. eps_1, eps_2 are analysis parameters. Originally stated assuming all means distinct; Appendix extends to cases where only the marginal arm L must be distinct.
